query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a ductile, high thermal conductivity metallic binder (e.g., silver) into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy matrix as a continuous phase will significantly improve mechanical integrity (compressive strength and resistance to cracking) without substantially diminishing the alloy's caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy, rare-earth-free, prone to cracking
generation.intervention: Form a composite by infiltrating or co-sintering the HEA with a continuous silver binder phase (e.g., 10–20 vol% Ag), ensuring percolation for mechanical support and heat transport.
generation.conditions: Applied magnetic field (up to 2 T), hydrostatic pressure (up to 1 GPa), temperature range 250–350 K, compressive loading up to 200 MPa
generation.structural_mediator: Continuous metallic binder phase (Ag) at grain boundaries and intergranular regions, providing ductility and thermal conductivity
generation.mechanism: The silver binder bridges cracks and distributes stress, increasing compressive strength and fracture resistance. Its high thermal conductivity enhances heat transport, while its non-magnetic nature and chemical inertness minimize interference with the magnetocaloric and barocaloric transitions of the HEA matrix.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compressive strength will increase to >200 MPa (matching or exceeding epoxy composites), thermal conductivity will increase by at least 5× relative to epoxy composites (approaching In composites), and caloric response (ΔS, ΔT) will remain within 90–100% of the original HEA value under field and pressure cycling.
generation.baseline: Unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 HEA, which cracks easily and has poor mechanical integrity; epoxy composites with 152–218 MPa strength but low thermal conductivity; In composites with 48 MPa strength and high thermal conductivity.
generation.boundary: Binder content must not exceed 20 vol% to avoid diluting caloric response; operation within 250–350 K, fields up to 2 T, pressures up to 1 GPa, compressive loads up to 200 MPa; rare-earth-free composition.
generation.uncertainty: The precise impact of Ag binder on caloric response is uncertain, as excessive binder may dilute active phase or alter transition characteristics; optimal binder fraction requires experimental tuning.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38–Ag composites with 10–20 vol% Ag. Measure compressive strength, thermal conductivity, and caloric response (ΔS, ΔT) under applied magnetic field and pressure, comparing to unmodified HEA and prior epoxy/In composites.
measurements: Caloric response: ΔS (J/kg·K), ΔT (K) under field and pressure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If compressive strength does not exceed 150 MPa, or caloric response drops below 80% of the original HEA value, the hypothesis is falsified.
